query: What praise and complaints appear in IMDb reviews?

per_column.name: praise_type
per_column.rationale: Praise is one of the two named halves of the concept 'praise and complaints'. Capturing the type/aspect of praise expressed is a constitutive part-of the concept — it is an aspect OF the audience reaction, not an external predictor of it.

per_column.name: complaint_type
per_column.rationale: Complaint is the other named half of the concept. Its type is a constitutive facet of audience_praise_and_complaints, decomposing the negative valence of the reaction.

per_column.name: subject_target
per_column.rationale: The target of the praise/complaint (film, actor, director, screenplay, etc.) is an intrinsic aspect of the reaction itself — every praise or complaint is about something. It is meronymic (the 'what it is about' dimension), not an external cause or predictor.

judge.rationale: All three columns are genuine constitutive facets of the concept, decomposing valence (praise vs. complaint) and target. However mutual exclusivity is weakened: praise_type and complaint_type draw from largely the SAME underlying value vocabulary (acting_performance, screenplay_writing, cinematography_visuals, direction, character-related aspects), so the 'aspect' dimension is duplicated across the two valence columns; furthermore subject_target overlaps heavily with the *_type columns (e.g., performance_actor / director / screenplay in subject_target restate acting_performance / direction / screenplay_writing in the type columns), so the same content-aspect is captured twice under different names. Exhaustiveness is fairly good: the type columns cover the main quality dimensions (acting, writing, visuals, direction, pacing, technical, originality, emotional impact) and the target column adds the object dimension, together spanning valence × aspect × target. What is not cleanly separated is intensity/strength of sentiment, but the core constitutive aspects of what praise and complaints consist of are largely covered.
